raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On gfx950, `TRITON_ATTN` now ranks right above `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` in ROCm attention auto-selection, for every model. This is a temporary workaround for #62606: unified attention gives wrong output on gfx950 for some KV cache sizes, and vLLM's aiter pin (v0.1.26) does not have the fix (ROCm/aiter#6661, released in aiter v0.1.27). Other GPUs are unchanged.

Related:
- #62606: the unified attention bug on gfx950.
- #61433 (draft, paused): ranks unified attention above `ROCM_ATTN` for spec decode and hybrid models, for performance. It removes this rule after the pin bump.

## Claims

- On gfx950, runs that do not get `ROCM_ATTN` (KV connector runs, encoder-decoder models, layers `ROCM_ATTN` cannot serve) select `TRITON_ATTN` instead of unified attention. This avoids the wrong output from #62606 until the aiter pin includes ROCm/aiter#6661.
- Nothing else changes. `ROCM_ATTN` stays first, `ROCM_AITER_FA` stays first when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, and unified attention still works when selected with `--attention-backend`.

Resulting order of the three backends on gfx950:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | `ROCM_ATTN` > unified > `TRITON_ATTN` | `ROCM_ATTN` > `TRITON_ATTN` > unified |
| with a KV connector (`ROCM_ATTN` excluded) | unified > `TRITON_ATTN` | `TRITON_ATTN` > unified |

## Validation

**Accuracy.** One MI355X (gfx950), temperature 0. GSM8K is 5-shot over all 1319 questions. MRCR is `tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py` with 30 samples of 16k–33k tokens. The setup is in #62606. The Qwen3-32B rows come from #62606. The Qwen3-8B rows were retested on 2026-10-27 on main `00b6c4c565` with aiter v0.1.26 and v0.1.27.

| model, KV per layer | benchmark | `TRITON_ATTN` | unified attention, pinned aiter (no fix) | unified attention, aiter with the fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-32B, default settings, 2.7 GiB | GSM8K, first run (low blocks only) | 0.744 | 0.749 | 0.751 |
| | MRCR | 0.478 | **0.327** | 0.502 |
| | GSM8K, second run | 0.738 | **0.633** | 0.733 |
| Qwen3-8B, 3.97 GiB, after 525k filler tokens | GSM8K | 0.860 | **0.004** | 0.864 (v0.1.27) |
| | MRCR | 0.497 | **0.157** | 0.486 (v0.1.27) |

With spec decode (Qwen3-32B + EAGLE3, 2.5 GiB per layer), unified attention has a max error of 0.49 against an fp32 reference; `TRITON_ATTN` has 0.009. End to end, EAGLE3 acceptance length with unified attention and aiter v0.1.26 is 1.70, both at 1k input / concurrency 64 and at 8k / 16. With `TRITON_ATTN`, or with aiter v0.1.27, it is 2.31 and 2.11.

**Tests.** In `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`, `test_auto_selection_for_kv_connector` now also covers gfx950. With aiter there, a KV connector run selects `TRITON_ATTN`; without aiter it selects `TRITON_ATTN` on both architectures. The test runs in the attention CI step.

With a source build of this branch, run `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py`. Against the image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b`, apply this PR's `vllm/` diff to the installed package. Then run pytest from outside the checkout, so that the uncompiled source tree is not imported. On gfx950 at `68853bdcbf` this gives 65 passed and 17 deselected. All 82 tests in the file pass when run against the source tree.

```bash
cd /tmp && python3 -m pytest -q --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider --import-mode=importlib --rootdir /tmp \
  /work/vllm/tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py -k "not segmented and not deepseek"
```

## Details

**Root cause.** On gfx950, unified attention gives wrong output when a layer's KV cache is 2–4 GiB (#62606). Requests whose KV sits in blocks past 2 GiB get attention output unrelated to their context. With prefix caching on (the default), a server reaches those blocks once about 2 GiB per layer has been allocated in total. The fix is in aiter (ROCm/aiter#6661), so vLLM gets it only with a pin bump.

**Change.** A self-contained step at the end of `_get_backend_priorities`, so that it is easy to revert:

```python
# TODO(#62606): remove once the aiter pin includes ROCm/aiter#6661.
# ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN gives wrong output on gfx950 for some KV cache
# sizes, so rank TRITON_ATTN right above it there.
unified = AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
if on_gfx950() and unified in backends:
    backends.remove(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
    backends.insert(backends.index(unified), AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
```

**Tradeoff.** Where this applies, unified attention with aiter v0.1.27 is faster than `TRITON_ATTN`, mostly at long context:
- Qwen3-32B + EAGLE3: 3928 vs 3553 tok/s at 1k c64, and 856 vs 557 at 8k c16.
- Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B + MTP: 403 vs 207 tok/s at 64k c8.

With the current v0.1.26 pin, unified attention is not correct for every KV cache size, so `TRITON_ATTN` is the safe choice until the pin bump. #61433 restores the order after it.

**History.** An earlier version of this PR also ranked `ROCM_ATTN` last for spec decode and hybrid models, because its Triton fallback had two accuracy bugs. Both are now fixed on main:
- The sliding-window NaN (#62828) no longer occurs since #60767.
- #63268 fixed the unwritten output heads on gfx942.

What remained was a performance change, which belongs in #61433, so it was dropped from this PR.

**Author review.** I have reviewed the code changes and this description by hand.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

</details>

@simondanielsson Thanks for the review!

**Selection logic.** Close, with two corrections. The condition is spec decode **or** a hybrid model, not both. And on gfx950 `ROCM_ATTN` is last, not second. For the three backends:

| | gfx950 | gfx942 and others |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spec decode or hybrid | `TRITON_ATTN` > unified > `ROCM_ATTN` | unified > `TRITON_ATTN` > `ROCM_ATTN` |
| other models | `ROCM_ATTN` > `TRITON_ATTN` > unified | unchanged: `ROCM_ATTN` > unified > `TRITON_ATTN` |

So the net diffs are:
1. Spec decode or hybrid: `ROCM_ATTN` moves to the end (all GPUs).
2. gfx950 only: `TRITON_ATTN` moves right above unified attention (all models). For a plain dense model `ROCM_ATTN` is still first, so this only changes runs where `ROCM_ATTN` is excluded or last: KV connector runs, spec decode and hybrid models.

`ROCM_AITER_FA` stays first when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, as on main.

**Special case.** Done in d83b437c6f, see the inline reply.

**Description.** The "Evidence" section is now one table: hardware, model, spec decode, workload, backend before and after, and the result. Everything was measured on MI355X (gfx950). I have not measured gfx942; there the PR moves spec decode and hybrid models from `ROCM_ATTN` to unified attention, which matches the gfx950 results with the aiter fix, but it is not measured on gfx942.

```python
# ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN gives wrong output on gfx950 for some KV cache
# sizes, so rank TRITON_ATTN right above it there.
unified = AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
if on_gfx950() and unified in backends:
    backends.remove(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
    backends.insert(backends.index(unified), AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
```

**Tradeoff.** Where this applies, unified attention with aiter v0.1.27 is faster than `TRITON_ATTN`, mostly at long context:
- Qwen3-32B + EAGLE3: 3928 vs 3553 tok/s at 1k c64, and 856 vs 557 at 8k c16.
- Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B + MTP: 403 vs 207 tok/s at 64k c8.

With the current v0.1.26 pin, unified attention is not correct for every KV cache size, so `TRITON_ATTN` is the safe choice until the pin bump. #61433 restores the order after it.

**History.** An earlier version of this PR also ranked `ROCM_ATTN` last for spec decode and hybrid models, because its Triton fallback had two accuracy bugs. Both are now fixed on main:
- The sliding-window NaN (#62828) no longer occurs since #60767.
- #63268 fixed the unwritten output heads on gfx942.

What remained was a performance change, which belongs in #61433, so it was dropped from this PR.

**Author review.** I have reviewed the code changes and this description by hand.

@simondanielsson Thanks for the review!

**Selection logic.** Close, with two corrections. The condition is spec decode **or** a hybrid model, not both. And on gfx950 `ROCM_ATTN` is last, not second. For the three backends:

| | gfx950 | gfx942 and others |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spec decode or hybrid | `TRITON_ATTN` > unified > `ROCM_ATTN` | unified > `TRITON_ATTN` > `ROCM_ATTN` |
| other models | `ROCM_ATTN` > `TRITON_ATTN` > unified | unchanged: `ROCM_ATTN` > unified > `TRITON_ATTN` |

So the net diffs are:
1. Spec decode or hybrid: `ROCM_ATTN` moves to the end (all GPUs).
2. gfx950 only: `TRITON_ATTN` moves right above unified attention (all models). For a plain dense model `ROCM_ATTN` is still first, so this only changes runs where `ROCM_ATTN` is excluded or last: KV connector runs, spec decode and hybrid models.

`ROCM_AITER_FA` stays first when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, as on main.

**Special case.** Done in d83b437c6f, see the inline reply.

**Description.** The "Evidence" section is now one table: hardware, model, spec decode, workload, backend before and after, and the result. Everything was measured on MI355X (gfx950). I have not measured gfx942; there the PR moves spec decode and hybrid models from `ROCM_ATTN` to unified attention, which matches the gfx950 results with the aiter fix, but it is not measured on gfx942.

@tjtanaa would be great to have your view on this. Basically, changing default backends in some cases: >

@simondanielsson @tpopp I narrowed this PR to the gfx950 rule only (b2c4f380a8) and updated the title and description.

## **Dropped: ranking `ROCM_ATTN` last for spec decode and hybrid models.** 
Its motivation was accuracy, and both bugs in `ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton fallback are now fixed on main. The sliding-window NaN (#62828) no longer occurs since #60767 nulls the below-window block-table entries: at 8k input / concurrency 16, DFlash2 acceptance length on main is 3.22, and 1.19 with only #60767 reverted. The unwritten output heads on gfx942 were fixed by #63268. What remains is a performance gain, and that belongs in #61433. I am closing #62415 for the same reason.
## **Kept: `TRITON_ATTN` right above unified attention on gfx950** (#62606). 
`ROCM_ATTN` stays first, so this only changes runs that do not get `ROCM_ATTN`, for example KV connector runs. With the current aiter pin (v0.1.26), unified attention there gives GSM8K 0.004 vs 0.860 for `TRITON_ATTN` on the Qwen3-8B check in the description. aiter v0.1.27 has the fix (0.864). Once `AITER_BRANCH` moves to v0.1.27, #61433 removes this rule.

cc @tjtanaa: the default-order change you were asked about is now limited to that gfx950 rule.

vLLM main now pins aiter v0.1.27 (#63774), which contains the #62606 fix (ROCm/aiter#6661). The gfx950 rule here is no longer needed, so I am closing this PR. The remaining priority change continues in #61433.
